Q1 - One-section-at-a-time behavior: Do you want the page to always behave like tabs, with exactly one section visible at any moment, or should desktop keep a “show all” experience and only narrow screens use tabs?
-> Recommended answer: always one section visible; no show-all mode.

---

Q2 - Navigation shape on phones: With no CSS allowed, should the section names become a simple vertical list of tappable items, or do you want a different native control like a dropdown/select?
-> Recommended answer: a vertical list of tappable section names.

---

Q3 - Active-section indicator: What visible cue should mark the current section in the nav so it’s obvious without styling—e.g. “(current)”, a leading arrow, or some other text marker?
-> Recommended answer: use a plain text marker such as “(current)”, plus `aria-current` for accessibility.

---

Q4 - URL/hash behavior: Should clicking a section still update and honor the `#about` / `#contact` style hash so direct links and reloads open the right section?
-> Recommended answer: yes, preserve hash behavior.

Task: # Make the portfolio usable on a phone

The doctor's page in `index.html` shows its entire content stack at once. On a
phone you have to scroll through everything to reach the contact form, and the
navigation is one row of five links that wraps badly on a narrow screen.

Make the page behave like a tabbed page:

- the navigation should read as a list of section names, and the section you
  are currently looking at should be obvious;
- clicking a section name shows that section and hides the others;
- the page should be usable at a narrow phone width;
- the contact form must keep working exactly as it does now.

`script.js` already has section-toggling logic — build on it rather than
replacing it.

Constraints:

- plain HTML and JavaScript only;
- no CSS at all: no `.css` file, no `<style>` block, no `style="..."`
  attributes, no stylesheet link or CDN asset;
- no dependencies and no build step — the page is opened straight from disk;
- do not change the wording of the medical content;
- do not edit `.factory/` or `factory.yaml`.

The repository checks configured in `.factory/config.yaml` (`node --check
script.js` and `node tests/verify-page.mjs`) must keep passing.

Q1 - One-section-at-a-time behavior: Do you want the page to always behave like tabs, with exactly one section visible at any moment, or should desktop keep a “show all” experience and only narrow screens use tabs?
-> Recommended answer: always one section visible; no show-all mode.

---

Q2 - Navigation shape on phones: With no CSS allowed, should the section names become a simple vertical list of tappable items, or do you want a different native control like a dropdown/select?
-> Recommended answer: a vertical list of tappable section names.

---

Q3 - Active-section indicator: What visible cue should mark the current section in the nav so it’s obvious without styling—e.g. “(current)”, a leading arrow, or some other text marker?
-> Recommended answer: use a plain text marker such as “(current)”, plus `aria-current` for accessibility.

---

Q4 - URL/hash behavior: Should clicking a section still update and honor the `#about` / `#contact` style hash so direct links and reloads open the right section?
-> Recommended answer: yes, preserve hash behavior.

Q1 - One-section-at-a-time behavior: Do you want the page to always behave like tabs, with exactly one section visible at any moment, or should desktop keep a “show all” experience and only narrow screens use tabs?
-> Recommended answer: always one section visible; no show-all mode.

---

Q2 - Navigation shape on phones: With no CSS allowed, should the section names become a simple vertical list of tappable items, or do you want a different native control like a dropdown/select?
-> Recommended answer: a vertical list of tappable section names.

---

Q3 - Active-section indicator: What visible cue should mark the current section in the nav so it’s obvious without styling—e.g. “(current)”, a leading arrow, or some other text marker?
-> Recommended answer: use a plain text marker such as “(current)”, plus `aria-current` for accessibility.

---

Q4 - URL/hash behavior: Should clicking a section still update and honor the `#about` / `#contact` style hash so direct links and reloads open the right section?
-> Recommended answer: yes, preserve hash behavior.

Q1 - One-section-at-a-time behavior: Do you want the page to always behave like tabs, with exactly one section visible at any moment, or should desktop keep a “show all” experience and only narrow screens use tabs?
-> Recommended answer: always one section visible; no show-all mode.

---

Q2 - Navigation shape on phones: With no CSS allowed, should the section names become a simple vertical list of tappable items, or do you want a different native control like a dropdown/select?
-> Recommended answer: a vertical list of tappable section names.

---

Q3 - Active-section indicator: What visible cue should mark the current section in the nav so it’s obvious without styling—e.g. “(current)”, a leading arrow, or some other text marker?
-> Recommended answer: use a plain text marker such as “(current)”, plus `aria-current` for accessibility.

---

Q4 - URL/hash behavior: Should clicking a section still update and honor the `#about` / `#contact` style hash so direct links and reloads open the right section?
-> Recommended answer: yes, preserve hash behavior.

Task: # Make the portfolio usable on a phone

The doctor's page in `index.html` shows its entire content stack at once. On a
phone you have to scroll through everything to reach the contact form, and the
navigation is one row of five links that wraps badly on a narrow screen.

Make the page behave like a tabbed page:

- the navigation should read as a list of section names, and the section you
  are currently looking at should be obvious;
- clicking a section name shows that section and hides the others;
- the page should be usable at a narrow phone width;
- the contact form must keep working exactly as it does now.

`script.js` already has section-toggling logic — build on it rather than
replacing it.

Constraints:

- plain HTML and JavaScript only;
- no CSS at all: no `.css` file, no `<style>` block, no `style="..."`
  attributes, no stylesheet link or CDN asset;
- no dependencies and no build step — the page is opened straight from disk;
- do not change the wording of the medical content;
- do not edit `.factory/` or `factory.yaml`.

Q1 - One-section-at-a-time behavior: Do you want the page to always behave like tabs, with exactly one section visible at any moment, or should desktop keep a “show all” experience and only narrow screens use tabs?
-> Recommended answer: always one section visible; no show-all mode.

---

Q2 - Navigation shape on phones: With no CSS allowed, should the section names become a simple vertical list of tappable items, or do you want a different native control like a dropdown/select?
-> Recommended answer: a vertical list of tappable section names.

---

Q3 - Active-section indicator: What visible cue should mark the current section in the nav so it’s obvious without styling—e.g. “(current)”, a leading arrow, or some other text marker?
-> Recommended answer: use a plain text marker such as “(current)”, plus `aria-current` for accessibility.

---

Q4 - URL/hash behavior: Should clicking a section still update and honor the `#about` / `#contact` style hash so direct links and reloads open the right section?
-> Recommended answer: yes, preserve hash behavior.
